title: Springboard activation scorecard and ramp manifest
body:
Purpose
This working doc captures the minimum acceptance scorecard, phased ramp manifest, and surge contingencies for feature activations that require coordinated infra, model, and go-to-market steps. Intended for product-ops, release engineering, SRE, and solutions engineering leads.

Summary / TL;DR
- Goal: safe 4-week ramp from 0 -> 100% activation for voice-notes feature with staged cohorts.
- Primary KPIs to gate each phase: 99th percentile latency SLO, error-rate, token-cost per 1k, customer satisfaction (CSAT), and model-quality pass-rate on sentinel prompts.
- Hard gates: if any phase breaches latency or error thresholds for 2 consecutive days, rollback to previous cohort and trigger triage.
- Secondary controls: traffic shaping, canary token caps, autoscale buffer + burst pool, model-fallback routing to smaller quantized variant.

Activation phases (high level)
Phase 0 — Dry run (internal 0.1%)
- Duration: 3 days.
- Audience: internal staff + closed beta.
- Objectives: exercise runtime deployment, routing, KV-cache warmup patterns, billing telemetry.
- Gate: 99th pctl latency < 650ms, error-rate < 0.5%, model-quality pass-rate >= 96% on sentinel set.

Phase 1 — Early customers (1%)
- Duration: 7 days.
- Audience: selected customers (contracted).
- Objectives: validate autoscale triggers, billing reconciliation, and prompt-set edge cases.
- Gate: 99th pctl latency < 600ms, error-rate < 0.3%, token-cost per 1k within +15% of forecast, CSAT >= 9/10 for pilot users.

Phase 2 — Expanded beta (10%)
- Duration: 7–10 days.
- Audience: broader opt-in cohort.
- Objectives: measure batching benefits, cache hit-rate targets, and quality drift.
- Gate: 99th pctl latency < 550ms, error-rate < 0.25%, model-quality pass-rate >= 94%, cache hit-rate >= 60%.

Phase 3 — Ramp to scale (50%)
- Duration: 4 days gradual ramp to 50%.
- Objectives: scale autoscaling, validate cost model, observe regional routing.
- Gate: 99th pctl latency < 500ms, error-rate < 0.2%, token-cost per 1k within +10% of forecast.

Phase 4 — Full activation (100%)
- Duration: 5 days final ramp.
- Objectives: steady-state monitoring and final handoff to bizops.
- Gate: stable metrics for 72 hours, all alerts green, adoption metrics trending healthy.

Scorecard (per-phase minimal tracked fields)
- date-range: string
- cohort-id: string
- traffic-%: string
- p50_latency_ms: string
- p95_latency_ms: string
- p99_latency_ms: string
- error_rate_pct: string
- cache_hit_rate_pct: string
- tokens_per_1k_cost_usd: string
- model_quality_pass_pct: string
(We expect teams to track this in the shared sheet; columns above are the canonical set used by Readout.)

KPI definitions (operational clarity)
- p99_latency_ms: measured at API ingress after auth checks, excluding streaming client-side latencies. Use server-side tracer.
- error_rate_pct: 100 * (5xx + model-timeout + validation-failures) / total_requests. Client aborts excluded.
- cache_hit_rate_pct: percentage of requests served with a valid prefix/KV cache that avoided full model forward pass.
- model_quality_pass_pct: fraction of sentinel prompts whose top-N outputs match expected intent/labels in automated eval harness.
- tokens_per_1k_cost_usd: blended cost computed from infra+model unit economics normalized to 1k tokens. Includes batching amortization.

Runbook & immediate triage steps (if gate breached)
1) Pager alert triggers SRE & product-ops.
2) Product-ops runs quick triage checklist: identify scope (region, model, route), severity (impact % of active users), and correlate to recent rollouts/PRs.
3) If p99 latency breach: enable temporary traffic shaping (max concurrency per tenant), increase autoscale target + allocate burst GPUs from Dedicated burst pool.
4) If error-rate spike: switch route to model-fallback (smaller quantized variant) and enable additional logging (sampling 1%) for failing requests.
5) If model-quality drop: initiate quick rollback to previous model version and run targeted eval on sentinel prompt partition A/B.
6) Communications: product ops drafts incident note and sends to #product-launch channel and stakeholders list.

Decision matrix (go/no-go signals)
- Strong go: All gates within tolerance for 48h and positive trends in cost and CSAT.
- Soft go: Transient noise in one secondary metric but primary SLOs held — proceed with caution + reduced ramp rate.
- No-go: Any primary SLO (p99 latency, error-rate, model-quality) breaches for >=2 days or shows monotonic worsening despite mitigations.

Operational checklist (pre-phase 0 -> phase 1 handoff)
- Infra: autoscale policies reviewed and tested, burst pool verified, KMS keys available for private routes.
- Models: model pinned with version tag, quantized fallback built and smoke-tested.
- Observability: dashboards created, alert thresholds set, synthetic probes active per region.
- Billing: cost forecasts uploaded and finance has pre-approved budget for burst usage.
- Docs: customer-facing enablement doc + opt-out flow published.
- Legal/Compliance: data retention and PII flows reviewed for beta cohort.
- Support: SRE on-call schedule added, CS playbook drafted.

Communication cadence during ramp
- Daily standup (15m) during phases 1–3 with product-ops, SRE, release engineering.
- Morning snapshot email to exec sponsor with 3 metrics and one critical risk.
- Weekly readout to GTM and CS with adoption and CSAT highlights.

Sample escalation templates (short forms for Slack/Email)
- Incident slack blurb: "ALERT: Phase 2 traffic at risk — p99 latency 620ms (target 550). Triage started: @oncall-sre @aisha.patel. Next update in 20m. Impact: ~10% of active users experiencing >500ms."
- Exec snapshot: one-line status, top-3 metrics, mitigation steps, expected next milestone.

Quality monitoring specifics (unique to feature)
- Sentinel prompt set: 150 prompts covering edge multilingual audio, profanity-handling, long-context stitching. Partition into A/B for canary validation.
- Automated regression harness runs hourly during ramp; failures >3% trigger model-quality alert.
- Manual spot-checks by solutions-engineering on daily cadence for first week of phase 1.

Cost control knobs and forecasting notes
- Batching policy: enable continuous batching with max latency budget per request = 40ms to avoid high p99 impact.
- Cache TTL tuning: aggressive prefix caching for repetitive prompts with 30s TTL, evaluate hit-rate after 2k requests.
- Model selection: prioritize high-throughput quantized variant for background processing; reserve full-precision for new-customer onboarding flows.
- Forecast template: provide per-phase estimated tokens, expected batch factor, and blended cost per 1k. Finance-snapshot link attached in linked_artifacts.

Open questions & TODOs (working notes)
- Confirm CS playbook wording for token-cost transparency. @Sofia to draft by 2026-03-04.
- Decide whether to enable region-based incremental ramping (EU-first then NA) — dependency on legal review.
- Run synthetic noisy-audio prompts to validate KV-cache seeding strategy.

Notes on provenance
This doc is an iterative working artifact — intended to be copied into the canonical product-ops ramp sheet and to seed a Confluence activation playbook. Keep changes annotated in the changelog section (next steps) rather than editing historical rows.

Next steps (immediate)
- Convert canonical scorecard columns to shared Google Sheet and wire to dashboards (assigned: Marco).
- Finalize sentinel prompt set and run 24h warmup synthetic load (assigned: Sofia).
- Finance to approve burst budget buffer (assigned: Ravi).
